rows.question: When does my maternity leave start if my due date is 15 November 2026?
rows.reply:
The Mutterschutz (statutory maternity protection period) before birth covers the last six weeks before delivery. MuSchG §3(1) says the employer may not employ a pregnant woman "in den letzten sechs Wochen vor der Entbindung" (the Schutzfrist vor der Entbindung). The only exception is if she expressly declares she is willing to work. She can withdraw that declaration at any time, with effect for the future.

The period is counted from the expected date of delivery shown on the certificate from a doctor, a midwife or an Entbindungspfleger: "der voraussichtliche Tag der Entbindung … wie er sich aus dem ärztlichen Zeugnis oder dem Zeugnis einer Hebamme oder eines Entbindungspflegers ergibt" (MuSchG §3(1)). So with an expected date of 15 November 2026, the period is the six weeks before that date. The excerpts set the period in weeks. They do not give a rule for counting it to an exact calendar day, so the starting day is not stated here.

If the baby is not born on the expected day, the period before birth becomes shorter or longer to match (MuSchG §3(1)).

After the birth, the employer may not employ the mother until eight weeks have passed (MuSchG §3(2)). This extends to twelve weeks in three cases:
1. premature births;
2. multiple births;
3. where a doctor finds a disability in the child, within the meaning of SGB IX §2(1) sentence 1, before the eight weeks end. This third extension applies only if the mother applies for it.

If the birth comes early, the period after birth is also extended by the time lost before birth. The twelve-week extension does not apply to a stillbirth (MuSchG §3(2)).

A pregnant woman should tell her employer about the pregnancy and the expected date of delivery as soon as she knows she is pregnant. If the employer asks, she should provide a certificate stating the expected date (MuSchG §15).

For Mutterschaftsgeld paid before the birth, the health insurer relies on the doctor's or midwife's certificate giving the expected date (SGB V §24i(3)). Your employer applies the employment ban. For payment questions about your own case, your Krankenkasse is the place to ask.

rows.question: How long after birth can we apply for Elterngeld without losing money?
rows.reply:
The law does not set an application deadline. It limits how far back Elterngeld (parental allowance) is paid.

Under BEEG §7(1), Elterngeld must be applied for in writing. It is paid retroactively only for the last three Lebensmonate before the start of the Lebensmonat in which the application is received: "rückwirkend nur für die letzten drei Lebensmonate vor Beginn des Lebensmonats geleistet, in dem der Antrag auf Elterngeld eingegangen ist." Months further back than that are not paid.

Under BEEG §4(1), Elterngeld can be drawn from the day of birth ("Es kann ab dem Tag der Geburt bezogen werden"). So no months are lost if the application arrives early enough for the three-month backdating to reach back to the first month you want paid. An application received later loses those earlier months of payment.

The excerpts do not define how a Lebensmonat is counted. Your Elterngeldstelle decides on Elterngeld applications, so that is where to ask how this applies to your own child's dates.

rows.question: How much notice do I have to give my employer for Elternzeit?
rows.reply:
Elternzeit (parental leave (unpaid job-protected leave)) is requested from your employer. The notice period depends on when the leave falls (BEEG §16(1)):

- For leave up to the child's third birthday: at least seven weeks before it starts ("spätestens sieben Wochen").
- For leave between the third birthday and the child's eighth birthday: at least 13 weeks before it starts ("spätestens 13 Wochen").

The request must be made "in Textform". The Familienportal explains that this means a letter without a signature or an email is also possible.

If you request leave for the period up to the third birthday, you must at the same time state which periods within two years you will take as Elternzeit. Where the mother takes Elternzeit directly after the maternity protection period under §3(2) and (3) of the Mutterschutzgesetz, that period counts toward this two-year period. If she takes it after annual leave that follows the maternity protection period, both the maternity protection period and the annual leave count toward it.

Shorter notice: the statute says that "bei dringenden Gründen ist ausnahmsweise eine angemessene kürzere Frist möglich" (for urgent reasons, a reasonable shorter period is possible as an exception). The Familienportal gives premature births and an adoption placement that could not be planned in time as examples. It says the period that applies in such cases depends on the circumstances of the individual case. Separately, under BEEG §16(2), if a mother cannot request on time, for a reason she is not responsible for, Elternzeit that follows directly after the maternity protection period, she can make the request within one week after that reason ends.

Other points in the same rules:

- Your employer must confirm your Elternzeit to you in writing ("Der Arbeitgeber hat ... die Elternzeit zu bescheinigen", BEEG §16(1)).
- Protection against dismissal starts from the time Elternzeit is requested. It begins no earlier than eight weeks before leave up to the third birthday, and no earlier than 14 weeks before leave between the third and eighth birthdays (BEEG §18(1)).

Older births: the Familienportal states that for births before 1 July 2015 the notice is seven weeks in all cases, including leave after the third birthday. The statutory transitional provision behind this is not among these excerpts.

rows.question: How long is maternity protection after the birth if the baby comes early?
rows.reply:
Under MuSchG §3(2), an employer may not employ a woman until eight weeks after the birth ("bis zum Ablauf von acht Wochen nach der Entbindung"). This is the period after birth of Mutterschutz (statutory maternity protection period).

If the baby comes early, two rules can apply.

1. Born before the expected date. The period after birth is extended by the days lost from the six-week period before birth ("verlängert sich die Schutzfrist nach der Entbindung ... um den Zeitraum der Verkürzung der Schutzfrist vor der Entbindung"). The guidance page describes this as a total that still comes to 14 weeks, ending as many days after the eight weeks as the baby arrived before the expected date.

2. Premature birth ("Frühgeburt"). The period after birth is extended to twelve weeks. The days lost before birth are added on top of these twelve weeks. MuSchG §3(2) does not define Frühgeburt. The guidance page gives one example of when a baby counts medically as premature: a birth weight under 2,500 grams. It says the total period then rises from 14 to 18 weeks.

The statute extends the period after birth to twelve weeks in three cases:
1. premature births ("bei Frühgeburten");
2. multiple births ("bei Mehrlingsgeburten");
3. where a doctor finds a disability in the child, within the meaning of § 2(1) sentence 1 SGB IX, before eight weeks after the birth have passed.

The extension for the third case applies only if the woman applies for it. The guidance page says this application is made to the health insurance fund (Krankenkasse). The twelve-week extension does not apply to a stillbirth.

After the birth, an employer may not employ the woman during this period. The guidance page says that if an employer demands work during the protection period, she can turn to the supervisory authority (Aufsichtsbehörde). One exception applies to school and university students. Their place of study may let them take part in their studies during the period after birth if they expressly ask for this. They can withdraw that request at any time.

rows.question: Can my employer dismiss me while I am pregnant?
rows.reply:
Only in exceptional cases, and only with an authority's approval.

The rule. Under MuSchG §17(1), dismissal of a woman is not permitted ("Die Kündigung gegenüber einer Frau ist unzulässig"):
1. during her pregnancy,
2. until four months after a miscarriage after the twelfth week of pregnancy, and
3. until the end of her protection period after the birth, and at least until four months after the birth.

This Kündigungsschutz (protection against dismissal) applies if the employer knows of the pregnancy, the miscarriage or the birth when dismissing, or is told within two weeks of the dismissal being received ("innerhalb von zwei Wochen nach Zugang der Kündigung"). Missing the two weeks does no harm if the reason is not the woman's fault and she informs the employer without delay ("unverzüglich"). The same rules apply to steps an employer takes to prepare a dismissal. The Familienportal adds that the protection applies even if you did not yet know you were pregnant, but you must already have been pregnant when you received the dismissal.

The exception. Under MuSchG §17(2), the highest state authority responsible for occupational safety, or a body it designates, may exceptionally declare a dismissal permissible. This is only for special cases not connected to the woman's condition during pregnancy, after a miscarriage after the twelfth week, or after the birth. The dismissal must be in writing and must state the reason. The Familienportal gives these examples of special grounds: the company is insolvent, part of the business is being closed, a small business cannot continue without a qualified replacement, or a particularly serious breach of duty. In these cases the employer must make a written application to the Aufsichtsbehörde. The Familienportal describes it as the authority responsible for compliance with the Mutterschutzgesetz. Without its approval, the dismissal is ineffective ("unwirksam").

If you are dismissed without that approval. The Familienportal says you must bring an action (Klage) before the competent Arbeitsgericht to have the dismissal declared legally ineffective. It says the action must "normalerweise innerhalb von 3 Wochen" be brought from receipt of the written dismissal. If no action is brought, the dismissal is treated as effective ("gilt die Kündigung Ihres Arbeitgebers als rechtswirksam"). You can bring the action yourself, through a representative such as a lawyer, or orally on record at the court office ("mündlich zu Protokoll der Geschäftsstelle"). The page also says you should involve the Aufsichtsbehörde.

If you are dismissed with that approval, you can also challenge the approval. Depending on the Bundesland, this is done by an objection (Widerspruch) or by bringing an action. That is a separate procedure. It does not replace the action at the Arbeitsgericht and cannot on its own preserve your employment. The excerpts do not say which of the two applies in Hessen.

After the birth. If you take Elternzeit, the protection can be extended. BEEG §18(1) says the employer may not dismiss you from the point at which Elternzeit has been requested, and not during Elternzeit. This protection begins at the earliest eight weeks before Elternzeit taken before the child's third birthday. For Elternzeit between the third birthday and the end of the child's eighth year, it begins at the earliest 14 weeks before. Here too, a dismissal can be declared permissible only exceptionally, by the state occupational-safety authority or a body it designates.

On fixed-term contracts, the Familienportal says maternity protection applies while the contract runs and ends when the contract ends.

Whether a particular dismissal is permissible is decided by the Aufsichtsbehörde, and its effectiveness by the Arbeitsgericht. The Aufsichtsbehörde for your area is where to take questions about your own situation.

rows.question: Is there an income limit above which we get no Elterngeld?
rows.reply:
Yes. Under BEEG §1(8), the entitlement to Elterngeld (parental allowance) lapses ("Ein Anspruch entfällt") if the entitled person had a zu versteuerndes Einkommen (taxable income) under §2(5) of the Income Tax Act of more than 175,000 euros "im letzten abgeschlossenen Veranlagungszeitraum vor der Geburt des Kindes" (in the last completed tax assessment period before the birth).

If another person also meets the conditions of §1(1) sentence 1 no. 2 (living in one household with the child), or of §1(3) or §1(4), the two incomes are added together. In that case the entitlement lapses when the combined zu versteuerndes Einkommen of both persons is more than 175,000 euros.

The limit applies to taxable income, not gross income. The official family portal says gross income is usually considerably higher than taxable income. It also says that taxable income is determined by the Finanzamt and appears in the tax assessment notice (Steuerbescheid), and that this notice for the year before the birth should be attached to the Elterngeld application where it exists.

If the tax assessment notice for that period is not yet available at the time of application, BEEG §8 still applies. Under §8(2), where the application indicates the limit will probably not be exceeded, Elterngeld is paid subject to revocation if the limit turns out to be exceeded. Under §8(3) no. 1, where it cannot yet be stated whether the limit is exceeded, the amount is decided provisionally until the required information is provided.

The portal also describes different, higher limits for births before 1 April 2025. The statutory excerpts available here do not include the transitional provision that sets those earlier limits, so this reply does not say which limit governs a particular birth date.

The 175,000 euro limit is the only rule here that removes the entitlement altogether. Separately, the monthly amount is capped. BEEG §2(1) sets a maximum of 1,800 euros a month, and §2(3) counts pre-birth income at no more than 2,770 euros.

Whether the limit applies to your family is decided by the Elterngeldstelle that handles your application. That is where to ask about your own case.

rows.question: How many months of Elterngeld can we get in total?
rows.reply:
The total depends on which variant you choose and on a few conditions in the law. This is the general rule. It is not a calculation for your family.

Basic rule. Elterngeld (parental allowance) is granted as Basiselterngeld or as Elterngeld Plus (BEEG §4(1)). "Die Eltern haben gemeinsam Anspruch auf zwölf Monatsbeträge Basiselterngeld": parents are jointly entitled to 12 monthly payments of Basiselterngeld. If one parent's income from work is reduced in two Lebensmonate, the parents jointly get two further months of Basiselterngeld, called Partnermonate. That makes 14 (BEEG §4(3)).

Elterngeld Plus. Instead of one Lebensmonat of Basiselterngeld, a parent may take two Lebensmonate of Elterngeld Plus (BEEG §4(3)).

Limits per parent. One parent can receive at most 12 monthly payments of Basiselterngeld, plus at most four monthly payments of Partnerschaftsbonus under §4b. A parent is only entitled to Elterngeld if they take it for at least two Lebensmonate (BEEG §4(4)). §4b is not among the excerpts here. The Familienportal guidance page describes the Partnerschaftsbonus as up to 4 additional months of ElterngeldPlus for each parent, if both work part-time in parallel.

Time window. Elterngeld can be received from the day of birth. Basiselterngeld can be received until the child completes the 14th Lebensmonat. Elterngeld Plus can be received until completion of the 32nd Lebensmonat, as long as from the 15th Lebensmonat at least one parent takes it in consecutive Lebensmonate (BEEG §4(1)). For an adopted child, Elterngeld can be received from when the child is taken in, at the latest until the child completes its eighth year (BEEG §4(1)).

How months are counted. Elterngeld is paid in monthly amounts for the child's Lebensmonate (BEEG §4(2)). The Familienportal page says these are not calendar months. Their start depends on the day of birth. Its example: a child born on 15 February has a first Lebensmonat from 15 February to 14 March.

Months that count as used. Lebensmonate in which a parent receives benefits credited under §3(1) sentence 1 nos. 1 to 3 count as months of Basiselterngeld for that parent. The same applies to insurance benefits under §192(5) sentence 2 of the Versicherungsvertragsgesetz (BEEG §4(4)). The Familienportal page explains that for the mother this covers months with Mutterschaftsgeld or other maternity benefits for the same child.

Both parents at once. Both parents can receive Basiselterngeld at the same time only in one of the first twelve Lebensmonate (BEEG §4(6)). The Familienportal page says that in such a month, 2 Basiselterngeld months count as used. If one parent takes Elterngeld Plus, they may receive it alongside the other parent's Basiselterngeld or Elterngeld Plus. The one-month limit does not apply in four cases (BEEG §4(6)):
- multiple births
- premature births within §4(5)
- children with a disability within §2(1) sentence 1 SGB IX that a doctor has established
- children who trigger a Geschwisterbonus under §2a(1) with (2) sentence 3

Premature births. The joint entitlement to Basiselterngeld is higher if the child was born early (BEEG §4(5)):
- at least 6 weeks before the expected date of delivery: 13 monthly payments
- at least 8 weeks before: 14 monthly payments
- at least 12 weeks before: 15 monthly payments
- at least 16 weeks before: 16 monthly payments

In these four cases, the per-parent maximum rises to 13, 14, 15 or 16 monthly payments of Basiselterngeld respectively, plus at most four of Partnerschaftsbonus. Basiselterngeld can then be received until completion of the 15th, 16th, 17th or 18th Lebensmonat respectively. Elterngeld Plus still runs until completion of the 32nd Lebensmonat. At least one parent must take it in consecutive Lebensmonate from the 16th, 17th, 18th or 19th Lebensmonat respectively. The expected date of delivery is the one shown in the certificate from a doctor, midwife or Entbindungspfleger (BEEG §4(5)).

In the application, you state for which Lebensmonate you claim Basiselterngeld, Elterngeld Plus or Partnerschaftsbonus (BEEG §7(1)).

How many months your family actually receives is decided on your application by the responsible Elterngeld office (Elterngeldstelle). That office is where to ask about your own case.

rows.question: What is the Partnerschaftsbonus and who qualifies?
rows.reply:
The Partnerschaftsbonus (partnership bonus months) is an additional monthly amount of Elterngeld Plus. Each parent receives it for a Lebensmonat in which both parents work part-time within a set range (BEEG §4b(1)).

Who qualifies, under BEEG §4b(1)–(3):
- Both parents must work "nicht weniger als 24 und nicht mehr als 32 Wochenstunden im Durchschnitt des Lebensmonats", meaning at least 24 and at most 32 hours a week on average over the Lebensmonat. It is the monthly average that counts, not each single week (Familienportal).
- Both parents must meet the requirements of BEEG §1. The excerpts I have do not set out what §1 requires.
- Each parent can receive at most four monthly amounts, and only if each takes it for at least two Lebensmonate.
- The parents can take it only at the same time and in consecutive Lebensmonate ("nur gleichzeitig und in aufeinander folgenden Lebensmonaten").

If one parent has to take it alone, BEEG §4c(2) gives a single parent an entitlement to additional monthly amounts of Elterngeld Plus. This applies if that parent works 24 to 32 hours a week on average in at least two and at most four consecutive Lebensmonate, and one of the three grounds in §4c(1) applies:
1. the parent meets the conditions for the single-parent relief under §24b(1) and (3) of the Income Tax Act, and the other parent lives neither with them nor with the child;
2. care by the other parent would endanger the child's welfare within the meaning of §1666(1) and (2) of the Civil Code; or
3. care by the other parent is impossible, in particular because of serious illness or severe disability. Economic reasons and being prevented by other activities do not count.

If one of these grounds arises while both parents are already receiving the bonus, one parent can continue receiving it under §4c(2) (BEEG §4b(4)). The Familienportal also states that separated parents can receive the bonus.

If the hours turn out not to be met in some months, BEEG §4b(5) says the consecutive-months requirement still counts as met. The Familienportal explains the consequences:
- If either parent works under 24 or over 32 hours on average in a Lebensmonat, both lose the bonus for that month and must repay it.
- Other months are not affected, as long as the conditions were met in at least two Lebensmonate.
- A change in hours from what was planned must be reported to the Elterngeldstelle.

Other points from the Familienportal:
- The bonus can be taken before, between or after the other Elterngeld months, even if you otherwise receive only Basiselterngeld.
- It is calculated the same way as Elterngeld Plus. The page puts it at between 150 and 900 euros a month per parent, depending on income before the birth. The excerpt I was given carries no check date for these figures.
- This guidance describes the law for children born after August 2021. Different rules partly apply to children born before 1 September 2021, and the page refers those parents to their Elterngeldstelle.

Whether a particular family meets these conditions is decided by the Elterngeldstelle. That office is where to ask about your own case.

rows.question: We forgot to apply for Kindergeld. How far back will they pay?
rows.reply:
The law limits how far back Kindergeld (child benefit) is paid, counted from when your application arrives. Under EStG §70(1), Kindergeld that has been set is paid retroactively "nur für die letzten sechs Monate vor Beginn des Monats, in dem der Antrag auf Kindergeld eingegangen ist": only for the last six months before the start of the month in which the application is received. Months before that are not paid. The same subsection says the entitlement itself is not affected by this payment limit ("Der Anspruch auf Kindergeld … bleibt von dieser Auszahlungsbeschränkung unberührt").

The official family portal adds that retroactive payment requires that Kindergeld was due to you but not paid, for example because no application was made. It says to state in the application that you are applying retroactively and from when you want Kindergeld. Because the six months run back from the month the application arrives, every month you wait moves that window forward.

Under BKGG §9(1), Kindergeld must be applied for in writing at the responsible Familienkasse. The portal says the application can be made electronically or in writing, on the Familienkasse form, at the Familienkasse of your Agentur für Arbeit. Questions about applying can go to the free Bundesagentur für Arbeit service line, 0800 4 555530.

Whether Kindergeld was due to you, and for which months, is decided by the Familienkasse, which sets Kindergeld by formal decision and pays it (EStG §70(1)). That is where to take your own case.

rows.question: How much Kindergeld do we get per month for our first child?
rows.reply:
Kindergeld (child benefit) is set by statute at the same monthly amount for every child, including a first child: "Das Kindergeld beträgt monatlich für jedes Kind 259 Euro", which is 259 euros per month for each child (EStG §66(1); the same wording is in BKGG §6(1)). The check date for this figure is attached to the citations from the corpus record.

It is paid monthly from the start of the month in which the conditions for entitlement are met, until the end of the month in which they stop being met (EStG §66(2)). The amount rises when the tax allowances for children under §31 and §32(6) EStG are raised (EStG §66(3)).

This is the rule for everyone. It does not settle whether your family meets the conditions. The Familienkasse examines those conditions, so it is the place to ask about your own case. The official Kindergeld page links to the online Kindergeld application at the Bundesagentur für Arbeit.

rows.question: How quickly do we have to register the birth at the Standesamt?
rows.reply:
The birth must be reported to the Standesamt (civil registry office) for the place where the child was born "binnen einer Woche", within one week (PStG §18(1)).

The statute names two ways the report is made:
1. by the persons named in PStG §19 sentence 1, orally or in writing; or
2. by the institutions named in PStG §20 sentences 1 and 2, in writing.

People who report under route 1 must substantiate the birth ("glaubhaft zu machen"). If a child is stillborn, the report must be made no later than the third working day after the birth (PStG §18(1)).

The Familienportal explains how this works in practice:
- If your child was born in a hospital, birth centre or maternity clinic, the institution notifies the responsible Standesamt and sends it the "Geburtsbescheinigung".
- If your child was born at home, the midwife or doctor issues the Geburtsbescheinigung. You must then present it to the responsible Standesamt within one week.

A Familienportal checklist words the period as "innerhalb von 7 Werktagen" (within 7 working days). The statute says "binnen einer Woche", and the statute governs.

For other documents you may need to bring, the Familienportal points to the website of the Standesamt in the place where your child is born.

rows.question: Which Standesamt do we go to — the one where we live or where the hospital is?
rows.reply:
The Standesamt (civil registry office) for the place where your child is born, not the one where you live. The federal Familienportal says you must register your child "beim Standesamt anmelden, das für den Geburtsort des Kindes zuständig ist", the Standesamt responsible for the child's place of birth. So if your child is born in a hospital in another town, it is that town's Standesamt.

On timing, the same page says registration is "innerhalb 1 Woche" (within one week) after the birth. The portal's birth checklist puts it as "innerhalb von 7 Werktagen" (within 7 working days).

If your child is born in a hospital, birth centre or maternity clinic, the facility notifies the responsible Standesamt and sends it the Geburtsbescheinigung. You give the child's first name and surname to the facility, and it forwards them to the Standesamt. If you have not yet chosen a name, the portal says you must report it to the responsible Standesamt within one month. After that, the Standesamt must inform the family court, which then chooses one parent to decide the name.

If your child is born at home, a midwife or doctor issues the Geburtsbescheinigung, and you must present it to the responsible Standesamt within one week.

The Standesamt issues the birth certificate (Geburtsurkunde). It then registers your child with the Einwohnermeldeamt automatically. The other documents you need are listed on the website of the Standesamt in the place where your child is born.

These points come from the federal guidance portal. The excerpts do not include the statutory provision on which Standesamt is responsible. For anything about your own registration, ask the Standesamt for the place of birth.

rows.question: What do we need to bring to the Standesamt to register the birth?
rows.reply:
PStV §33 lists the documents the Standesamt (civil registry office) "soll verlangen" (should ask to see) when a birth is notified:

1. If the parents are married to each other: their marriage certificate, or a certified extract from the marriage register. Also their own birth certificates, if the details of the parents' birth registration are not shown on the marriage certificate. The marriage certificate must be shown even if the marriage has been dissolved.
2. If the parents are not married to each other: the mother's birth certificate. If paternity has already been acknowledged, also the declarations of acknowledgement and the father's birth certificate, and, where applicable, the declarations of joint parental custody ("Sorgeerklärungen").
3. An identity card, passport or other recognised passport substitute for the parents.
4. If the birth is notified orally: a certificate of the birth issued by a doctor, midwife or male midwife ("Entbindungspfleger"), insofar as they were present at the birth.

The Standesamt may also ask for further documents where it needs them to prove details (PStV §33).

The certificate of birth ("Geburtsbescheinigung"): the Familienportal says you need it to register. If your child was born in a hospital, birth centre or maternity clinic, the facility notifies the responsible Standesamt and sends the certificate. If your child was born at home, the midwife or doctor issues it, and you must present it to the responsible Standesamt within one week.

Where and when: the Familienportal says to register the child within one week at the Standesamt responsible for the place of birth. Its checklist page puts this as "innerhalb von 7 Werktagen" (within 7 working days).

If the parents are not German citizens: PStV §34 says that, to check whether the child acquired German citizenship by birth under § 4 Abs. 3 of the Staatsangehörigkeitsgesetz, the Standesamt asks at registration whether a parent holds an unlimited right of residence ("unbefristetes Aufenthaltsrecht"), or a residence permit under the EU–Switzerland free movement agreement as a Swiss national or their family member. It then obtains written information from the Ausländerbehörde and itself decides whether the child acquired German citizenship.

For any further documents, the Familienportal points to the website of the Standesamt in the town where your child is born. That office is also where to ask about your own registration.

rows.question: Does my Krankenkasse pay for a midwife?
rows.reply:
If you have statutory health insurance, the law gives you a right to midwife care. SGB V §24d, the statutory health insurance law, says an insured woman is entitled to medical care and to "Hebammenhilfe" during pregnancy, at the birth and after the birth. This includes the examinations to establish the pregnancy and the prenatal check-ups ("Untersuchungen zur Feststellung der Schwangerschaft und zur Schwangerenvorsorge").

Two limits and one extension in the same section:

- Midwife care after the birth ("im Hinblick auf die Wochenbettbetreuung") lasts until twelve weeks after the birth ("bis zum Ablauf von zwölf Wochen nach der Geburt").
- Anything beyond that needs a doctor's order ("bedürfen der ärztlichen Anordnung").
- If the mother cannot care for the child after the birth, the insured child has its own right to the midwife care that relates to the child.

The Familienportal puts it the same way: every woman with a Krankenkasse (statutory health insurer) is entitled to support from a Hebamme (midwife).

If you are privately insured, the Familienportal says you should check with your insurer beforehand which services it covers. The excerpts do not say what private insurers pay for midwife care.

The excerpts do not say how to find a midwife or how billing works. Your Krankenkasse or private insurer is the place to ask about your own cover.

rows.question: How long after the birth can I still see a midwife at the Krankenkasse's cost?

The rule is in the statutory health insurance law, SGB V §24d. An insured woman is entitled to midwife help ("Hebammenhilfe") during pregnancy, at the birth and after the birth.

rows.question: When are the first check-ups for the baby?
rows.reply:
The first Vorsorgeuntersuchung (routine preventive check-up) happens straight after birth. The Kinder-Richtlinie sets ten check-ups in the first six years. Each may only be used within its stated period, with a tolerance window ("Toleranzgrenze"). The times are counted in days, weeks or months of the child's life ("Lebenstag", "Lebenswoche", "Lebensmonat").

The check-ups in the first year:
- U1: "unmittelbar nach der Geburt". It should be done within the first 30 minutes after the birth ("innerhalb der ersten 30 Minuten nach der Geburt"). The U1 has no tolerance window. If no doctor is present at the birth but a midwife is, the midwife should carry it out.
- U2: 3rd–10th day of life ("3.-10. Lebenstag"). Tolerance: 3rd–14th day.
- U3: 4th–5th week of life ("4.-5. Lebenswoche"). Tolerance: 3rd–8th week.
- U4: 3rd–4th month of life. Tolerance: 2nd–4½th month.
- U5: 6th–7th month. Tolerance: 5th–8th month.
- U6: 10th–12th month. Tolerance: 9th–14th month.

The later check-ups:
- U7: 21st–24th month. Tolerance: 20th–27th.
- U7a: 34th–36th month. Tolerance: 33rd–38th.
- U8: 46th–48th month. Tolerance: 43rd–50th.
- U9: 60th–64th month. Tolerance: 58th–66th.

For premature babies the same periods apply ("Auch bei Frühgeborenen sind die Untersuchungszeiträume einzuhalten"). The early birth is taken into account when the results are assessed.

The Richtlinie also contains a temporary exception for U6 to U9. It applied only until three months after 31 March 2023.

The Gemeinsamer Bundesausschuss notes that the version it currently offers, in force since 1 January 2026, does not yet include a decision that took effect on 20 August 2026.

The Bundeszentrale für gesundheitliche Aufklärung (BzGA) sends parent letters by email for each upcoming U-check-up, including which documents to bring.

rows.question: What is Mutterschaftsgeld and when do I apply for it?
rows.reply:
What it is: Mutterschaftsgeld (maternity pay from the health insurer) is a payment for the protection periods before and after the birth and for the day of delivery itself ("für die Zeit der Schutzfristen vor und nach der Entbindung sowie für den Entbindungstag", MuSchG §19). Who pays it depends on how the woman is insured.

If she is a member of a statutory health insurance fund, she receives Mutterschaftsgeld under the rules of the Fifth Book of the Social Code (MuSchG §19(1)). Under SGB V §24i(1), it goes to female members who are entitled to sickness benefit if unable to work, or who are not paid wages because of the protection periods under §3 MuSchG. It also goes to women whose employment ends immediately before the protection period begins, if they were members of a health insurance fund on the last day of employment. For members who were employed, doing home work, or dismissed under §17(2) MuSchG at the start of the protection period, it equals the average net daily pay of the last three settled calendar months before the protection period, up to a maximum of 13 euros per calendar day (SGB V §24i(2)). Others receive it at the level of sickness benefit. The claim is suspended while she receives pay subject to contributions, earned income or holiday compensation, except one-off payments (SGB V §24i(4)).

If she is not a member of a statutory health insurance fund, she receives Mutterschaftsgeld paid by the federal government, up to 210 euros in total. It is paid on application ("auf Antrag") by the Bundesamt für Soziale Sicherung (MuSchG §19(2)).

Employer supplement: while employed, she also receives a supplement from her employer for the same periods. The supplement is the difference between 13 euros and her average net daily pay from the last three settled calendar months before the protection period (MuSchG §20(1)). If the employment ends by dismissal under §17(2) MuSchG, or the employer cannot pay because of insolvency, the body responsible for paying Mutterschaftsgeld pays the supplement instead (MuSchG §20(3)).

When it is paid: it is paid for the protection period under §3 MuSchG and the day of delivery (SGB V §24i(3)). The Familienportal says the protection periods "beginnen normalerweise 6 Wochen vor dem errechneten Geburtstermin und enden 8 Wochen nach der Geburt". For payment before the birth, the decisive document is a certificate from a doctor or midwife stating the expected date of delivery (SGB V §24i(3)).

When to apply: the excerpts do not set a date or period for applying. They say only that the payment for women without statutory health insurance is made on application by the Bundesamt für Soziale Sicherung. For statutory members, the Familienportal describes it as the Mutterschaftsgeld of the statutory health insurance funds. Ask your health insurance fund, or the Bundesamt für Soziale Sicherung if you are not statutorily insured, about timing and the application.

Effect on Elterngeld: Mutterschaftsgeld under SGB V and the employer supplement under MuSchG §20 are offset against Elterngeld for the period from the child's birth. The payment under MuSchG §19(2) is excluded from this offset (BEEG §3(1)).

rows.question: We are not married. Is my partner automatically the legal father?
rows.reply:
No. Under German law a man is not the legal father just because he is the mother's partner. BGB §1592 says the father of a child is the man who:
1. is married to the mother at the time of birth ("zum Zeitpunkt der Geburt mit der Mutter des Kindes verheiratet ist"),
2. has acknowledged paternity ("die Vaterschaft anerkannt hat"), or
3. has had his paternity established by a court under § 1600d BGB or § 182 Abs. 1 FamFG.

The Familienportal states that if he is not married to the mother at the time of birth, he must make a Vaterschaftsanerkennung (acknowledgement of paternity) to count as the legal father. It is voluntary and needs the mother's consent.

What the law attaches to it:
- It may be made before the child is born (BGB §1594(4)).
- It is not effective while another man's paternity exists (BGB §1594(2)). The Familienportal adds that if the mother is married to another man at the birth, her husband is the legal father, and no acknowledgement can be made. The exception is a divorce petition filed before the birth: then an acknowledgement can be made within one year of the divorce, with the consent of the mother and her husband, and takes effect at the earliest when the divorce is final. The Familienportal notes this part is being updated after a recent change in the law.
- It is invalid if made subject to a condition or a time limit (BGB §1594(3)).
- Its legal effects can only be relied on from the moment it becomes effective, unless the law provides otherwise (BGB §1594(1)).

Where: he must make the declaration in person at a competent office, for example the Jugendamt, a Standesamt, an Amtsgericht or a notary. The mother must also give her consent in person. The office certifies both. Depending on the Bundesland, it may cost a fee at a notary or Amtsgericht.

If he does not want to acknowledge paternity, or the mother does not consent, the child, the mother or the presumed biological father can apply to a court to establish paternity.

Acknowledging paternity does not by itself give him parental custody. If you are not married at the birth, the mother has custody from birth. For joint custody, both parents must also declare that they want to share it ("Sorgeerklärungen"), or a court must decide it. Marrying after the birth also creates joint custody. Your local Jugendamt is the office to ask about custody questions.

rows.question: How do unmarried parents get joint custody?
rows.reply:
If the parents are not married to each other when the child is born, the mother has parental custody from the birth. Under BGB §1626a(1), unmarried parents have joint custody in three cases: 1. when they both declare that they want to take on custody jointly (Sorgeerklärung (declaration of joint custody)); 2. when they marry each other; 3. insofar as the Familiengericht transfers custody to them jointly. Otherwise, the mother has custody (BGB §1626a(3)).

First, paternity must be legally established. According to the Familienportal, the other parent becomes the legally recognised father when he acknowledges the child as his own with the mother's consent, or when a court establishes paternity. Recognising paternity does not by itself give the father custody. One of the three routes above is still needed.

Sorgeerklärungen: both parents make the declarations, for example at the Jugendamt or before a notary. They can also be made before the child is born. When Sorgeerklärungen under BGB §1626a(1) No. 1 are made, an entry is made in the custody register kept by the Jugendamt (SGB VIII §58(1)).

Marriage: if the parents marry after the birth, joint custody also arises.

Court transfer: on the application of one parent, the Familiengericht transfers custody, or part of it, to both parents jointly if this does not conflict with the child's welfare ("wenn die Übertragung dem Kindeswohl nicht widerspricht"). If the other parent puts forward no reasons against joint custody and none are otherwise apparent, the law presumes that joint custody does not conflict with the child's welfare (BGB §1626a(2)). The Familienportal adds that in this case the reasons must be raised within a period set by the court, and the court decides in a simplified procedure without hearing the Jugendamt and without hearing the parents in person.

Parents who are not married to each other have a right to advice on making a Sorgeerklärung and on the option of a court transfer of joint custody (SGB VIII §18(2)). The Familienportal says your responsible Jugendamt advises on all questions of parental custody.

rows.question: Will our baby automatically be German if we are both Indian citizens?
rows.reply:
German Staatsangehörigkeit (citizenship) is not acquired from your nationality alone. The law sets out two routes by birth, and only the authority checks which applies to your child.

Through a parent: under StAG §4(1), a child acquires German Staatsangehörigkeit by birth "wenn ein Elternteil die deutsche Staatsangehörigkeit besitzt", meaning if a parent holds German citizenship.

Through birth in Germany to foreign parents: under StAG §4(3), a child of foreign parents born in Germany acquires German Staatsangehörigkeit if one parent meets both of these conditions:
1. has had lawful habitual residence in Germany for five years ("seit fünf Jahren rechtmäßig seinen gewöhnlichen Aufenthalt im Inland"), and
2. holds an "unbefristetes Aufenthaltsrecht", or, as a Swiss national or a family member of one, a residence permit under the 1999 EU–Switzerland free movement agreement.
Where a child acquires citizenship this way, it is entered in the birth register where the birth is recorded.

Who checks: under PStV §34, when the birth is notified, the Standesamt asks whether a parent holds an "unbefristetes Aufenthaltsrecht". If the details indicate this condition is met, or if no details are given or there is doubt, it obtains written information from the Ausländerbehörde on whether the details are correct and whether the parent had five years' lawful habitual residence at the time of the birth. The Standesamt then examines whether the child acquired German Staatsangehörigkeit by birth and records the result. That Standesamt is where to ask about your own child.

If the child does not acquire German Staatsangehörigkeit: AufenthG §33 sets out the child's residence position. A child born in Germany can be granted a residence permit ex officio if one parent holds an Aufenthaltserlaubnis, a Niederlassungserlaubnis or an Erlaubnis zum Daueraufenthalt – EU. If both parents, or the parent with sole custody, hold one of these at the time of birth, the residence permit is granted ex officio. If a parent holds a visa or may stay without a visa at the time of birth, the child's stay counts as permitted until the visa or the lawful visa-free stay ends.

rows.question: Does our newborn need a residence permit?
rows.reply:
The excerpts set out three situations for a child born in Germany to foreign parents. Which one applies to your child is decided by the authorities, not here.

1. A residence permit when a parent holds a residence title (AufenthG §33). A child born in Germany "kann … von Amts wegen eine Aufenthaltserlaubnis erteilt werden": the child may be granted an Aufenthaltserlaubnis (residence permit) on the authority's own initiative if one parent holds an Aufenthaltserlaubnis, a "Niederlassungserlaubnis" or an "Erlaubnis zum Daueraufenthalt – EU". If, at the time of birth, both parents hold one of these titles, or the parent with sole custody ("allein personensorgeberechtigte Elternteil") does, the child "wird … die Aufenthaltserlaubnis von Amts wegen erteilt": the permit is granted on the authority's own initiative.

2. A stay that counts as permitted when a parent holds a visa (AufenthG §33). If the mother or father holds a visa at the time of birth, or may stay without a visa, the child's stay "gilt bis zum Ablauf des Visums oder des rechtmäßigen visumfreien Aufenthalts als erlaubt". It counts as permitted until that visa or lawful visa-free stay ends.

3. German citizenship by birth (StAG §4). A child acquires German citizenship by birth if one parent is a German citizen (§4(1)). A child of foreign parents born in Germany acquires it if one parent meets both of these conditions (§4(3)):
- the parent has had their lawful habitual residence in Germany for five years ("seit fünf Jahren rechtmäßig seinen gewöhnlichen Aufenthalt im Inland"), and
- the parent holds an unlimited right of residence ("unbefristetes Aufenthaltsrecht"), or, as a Swiss national or a Swiss national's family member, an Aufenthaltserlaubnis under the EU–Switzerland free movement agreement of 21 June 1999.
The acquisition is entered in the birth register.

How this is checked when the birth is registered (PStV §34): the Standesamt asks for these details when the birth is reported. Where the conditions appear to be met, or the parents give no details, or the Standesamt doubts them, it obtains written information from the Ausländerbehörde. The Standesamt then examines whether the child acquired German citizenship and records the result.

rows.question: We are getting Mutterschaftsgeld. Does that reduce our Elterngeld?
rows.reply:
Yes. Under the law, Mutterschaftsgeld (maternity pay from the health insurer) is offset against Elterngeld (parental allowance). BEEG §3(1) lists the maternity benefits that are offset ("angerechnet") when they are due for the time from the day of the child's birth:

- Mutterschaftsgeld under the Fifth Book of the Social Code (statutory health insurance) or under the Second Act on Health Insurance for Farmers.
- The employer's top-up to Mutterschaftsgeld under MuSchG §20 ("Zuschuss zum Mutterschaftsgeld").
- Pay and allowances under civil-servant or military rules for a period of employment prohibition from the day of birth.

There is one exception. The one-off Mutterschaftsgeld of at most 210 euros, paid by the Bundesamt für Soziale Sicherung to women who are not members of a statutory health insurer (MuSchG §19(2)), is not offset (BEEG §3(1) No. 1(a)).

How the offset works, according to the federal family portal, for maternity benefits received for the same child:

- They are offset in full ("komplett auf das Elterngeld angerechnet").
- If the maternity benefits are higher than the Elterngeld, only the maternity benefits are paid. If the Elterngeld is higher, the difference is paid as Elterngeld on top of the maternity benefits.
- Months in which maternity benefits are received for the same child count as months of Basiselterngeld. One day of entitlement in that month is enough for this.
- Maternity benefits are calculated in days, so they are offset to the exact day. The statute says that if the income is due for only part of a Lebensmonat of the child, it is offset only against the corresponding part of the Elterngeld (BEEG §3(1)).

The 300-euro amount that BEEG §3(2) otherwise keeps free from offsetting does not apply where maternity benefits under §3(1) No. 1 to 3 are offset. This is set out in BEEG §3(2).

If the father claims Elterngeld while the mother is on maternity leave, the portal says the maternity benefits are not offset against his Elterngeld. They are offset only against the mother's Elterngeld.

These are the general rules. How much your own Elterngeld is reduced depends on your figures. The Elterngeld office responsible for you decides your application, so that is where to ask about your own case.

rows.question: Can I work while receiving Elterngeld?
rows.reply:
Yes. Under BEEG §1(1), one of the conditions for Elterngeld (parental allowance) is that the person "keine oder keine volle Erwerbstätigkeit ausübt": they do no paid work, or do not work full time.

BEEG §1(6) sets out when a person is not in full employment. It names three cases:
1. their working time does not exceed 32 hours a week on average over the Lebensmonat ("32 Wochenstunden im Durchschnitt des Lebensmonats");
2. they are employed for vocational training ("Beschäftigung zur Berufsbildung"); or
3. they work as a suitable Kindertagespflegeperson within the meaning of §§ 23 and 43 of the Eighth Book of the Social Code.

Under BEEG §1(6a), people who are temporarily not working also count as employed while they remain in an employment relationship or are self-employed.

Working affects the amount. Under BEEG §2(3), for Lebensmonate after the birth in which you have earnings that are on average lower than your earnings before the birth, Elterngeld is paid as the applicable percentage of the difference between the two. For this, pre-birth earnings are counted up to at most 2,770 euros. The difference is calculated separately for months of Basiselterngeld and months of Elterngeld Plus. The maximum of 1,800 euros a month in BEEG §2(1) refers to full Lebensmonate in which there are no earnings from work. Under BEEG §4(3), instead of one Lebensmonat of Basiselterngeld, a parent can take two Lebensmonate of Elterngeld Plus. The official Familienportal notes that Elterngeld Plus can be especially worthwhile if you work part time. It also says that if both parents work part time at the same time, the Partnerschaftsbonus may be relevant.

The application and later proof matter. Under BEEG §8:
- If your application gives expected earnings from work, you must prove your actual earnings for that period after the Bezugszeitraum ends (§8(1)).
- If your application says you expect no earnings, Elterngeld is paid subject to revocation in case you do have earnings after all (§8(2)).
- If your application says you expect earnings during the Bezugszeitraum, the amount is first decided provisionally (§8(3) no. 3).

The Familienportal lists, as proof of earnings while receiving Elterngeld, an employer's certificate of your working hours for employees, or your own declaration of your previous and current working hours if you are self-employed. It says your employer is obliged to issue the documents you need.

The Familienportal states that these explanations apply to children born after August 2021. For a child born before 1 September 2021, some different rules apply, and the portal refers you to your Elterngeldstelle.

Whether you qualify, and how much you would receive while working, is decided by your Elterngeldstelle. That is the office to ask about your own case.

rows.question: Where and how do we apply for Kindergeld?
rows.reply:
Where to apply: the Kindergeld (child benefit) application goes to the Familienkasse. Under BKGG §13(1), the competent Familienkasse is the one for the district where the entitled person has their residence ("Wohnsitz"). If they have no residence in Germany, it is the Familienkasse for the district of their habitual abode ("gewöhnlicher Aufenthalt"). If they have neither, it is the one for the district where they work. In all other cases, it is the Familienkasse Bayern Nord. That Familienkasse receives the application and decides on the claim, so it is also where to ask about your own case. The Familienportal says to submit the application to the Familienkasse of your Agentur für Arbeit, which is usually responsible for processing it.

How to apply: BKGG §9(1) says Kindergeld must be applied for in writing ("schriftlich zu beantragen"). Besides the entitled person, anyone with a legitimate interest in the payment may also make the application. The Familienportal says the application can be made electronically or in writing, using the Familienkassen form. You can fill it in online, then print and sign it. For newborn children, you can submit the application fully online with a valid ELSTER certificate, without printing or signing by hand. The application must include your tax identification number and your child's.

Who applies: under BKGG §3(1), Kindergeld is paid to only one person per child. If the child lives in the parents' shared household, the parents decide between themselves who is the entitled person (§3(2)). If they do not decide, the family court determines this on application.

Supporting documents: the Arbeitsagentur says that for a child under 18 you usually only need to give your own and your child's tax identification numbers. For a child born abroad or living abroad, submit a copy of the foreign birth certificate, or another official document that certifies the birth. Proof can be sent online to your Familienkasse. If more documents are needed, the Familienkasse will tell you, and give you a date to submit them by. Missing that date can delay the application or lead to it being rejected. For a child over 18, additional proof is needed. Under BKGG §9(2), the child is only still taken into account if the entitled person notifies that the conditions of §2(2) are met.

Late applications: according to the Familienportal, Kindergeld can be paid retroactively for up to 6 months, if it was due but not paid, for example because no application was made. Earlier months are not covered by that.

Questions about the application: the Bundesagentur für Arbeit has a free service number, 0800 4 555530.

rows.question: What are the Elterngeld rules for a self-employed parent in Bavaria?
rows.reply:
Bavaria is outside the states this product covers. It covers federal law, Hessen state procedures and the Indian consular track. For how Elterngeld (parental allowance) applications are handled in Bavaria, contact the office responsible for Elterngeld in Bavaria or the Bavarian state's official portal. That office decides individual cases, so it is also where to ask about your own. This product does not cover Bavarian procedures.

Elterngeld itself is federal law, set out in the BEEG. The federal rules below apply in Bavaria as everywhere else.

Self-employed income counts. Elterngeld is based on income from Erwerbstätigkeit (gainful work) before the birth. The law builds this from positive income from "nichtselbständiger Arbeit" (employment) and from "Land- und Forstwirtschaft, Gewerbebetrieb und selbständiger Arbeit" (farming and forestry, trade or business, and self-employed work). The income must be taxable in Germany. It is calculated "nach Maßgabe der §§ 2c bis 2f" (BEEG §2(1)). Of those sections, the excerpts include only §2c, which covers employment income. They do not include the provisions on how self-employed income is determined.

Amounts (BEEG §2):
- The basic rate is 67 percent of pre-birth income from work.
- It is paid up to a maximum of 1,800 euros a month for full Lebensmonate in which the person has no income from work.
- Where pre-birth income was below 1,000 euros, the percentage rises, up to 100 percent.
- Where pre-birth income was above 1,200 euros, the percentage falls, down to 65 percent.
- If you earn after the birth, Elterngeld is paid as that percentage of the difference between pre-birth and post-birth income. Pre-birth income counts at no more than 2,770 euros for this.
- The minimum is 300 euros, including for someone with no income from work before the birth.

Who is entitled (BEEG §1(1)). A person is entitled who:
1. has a residence or habitual abode in Germany,
2. lives in one household with the child,
3. cares for and brings up the child personally, and
4. does no work or does not work full time.

Under §1(6), a person is not working full time if:
1. their working time does not exceed 32 hours a week on average over the Lebensmonat,
2. they are in vocational training, or
3. they work as a qualified childminder.

Under §1(6a), people who are temporarily not working still count as working while they are "selbständig erwerbstätig" (self-employed).

Income limit (BEEG §1(8)). The claim lapses if the person had taxable income of more than 175,000 euros in the last completed Veranlagungszeitraum before the birth. Where another person also meets the household conditions, the limit applies to the sum of both persons' taxable income.

Provisional decisions (BEEG §8). The amount is decided provisionally, until the required information is proven, where:
1. at the time of the application, the tax assessment for the last completed Veranlagungszeitraum before the birth is not available and it cannot yet be said whether the §1(8) limit is exceeded,
2. income from work before the birth cannot be determined, or
3. the application states that the person expects to have income from work during the Bezugszeitraum.

Where the application gave expected income, the actual income must be proven after the Bezugszeitraum ends (§8(1)). Elterngeld is paid subject to revocation in two cases (§8(2)):
- the application says no income from work is expected during the Bezugszeitraum, or
- the tax assessment is not yet available and the application says the §1(8) limit is not expected to be exceeded.

Duration (BEEG §4). Elterngeld is paid as Basiselterngeld or Elterngeld Plus. Basiselterngeld can be drawn until the child completes the 14th Lebensmonat. Elterngeld Plus can be drawn until the 32nd Lebensmonat, as long as at least one parent draws it in consecutive Lebensmonate from the 15th. Parents together are entitled to twelve monthly amounts of Basiselterngeld. They get two more (Partnermonate) if one parent's income from work is reduced in two Lebensmonate. One Lebensmonat of Basiselterngeld can be taken as two Lebensmonate of Elterngeld Plus.

Whether you qualify, and how much you would receive, is decided only by the responsible Elterngeld office in Bavaria.

Whether your application will be approved is a decision on your family's own case, and this service cannot predict it. Only your Elterngeldstelle decides an Elterngeld (parental allowance) application.

What the law sets out for everyone:

- Under BEEG §1(1), a person is entitled to Elterngeld if they (1) have a residence or habitual abode in Germany, (2) live in one household with their child, (3) look after and bring up that child themselves, and (4) are not working, or not working full time. Under §1(6), a person is not working full time if, among other cases, their working time does not exceed "32 Wochenstunden im Durchschnitt des Lebensmonats" (32 hours a week on average over the month).
- Under BEEG §1(7), a foreign national without EU free-movement rights is entitled only if they hold one of the residence titles the provision lists, such as a settlement permit or an EU Blue Card.
- Under BEEG §1(8), the entitlement lapses if taxable income in the last completed assessment period before the birth was more than 175,000 euros. Where another person also meets the conditions, the combined taxable income of both people counts.
- Under BEEG §7(1), Elterngeld must be applied for in writing ("schriftlich zu beantragen"). It is paid retroactively only for the last three months before the month in which the application is received, so a late application loses earlier months of payment.

Which side of these conditions your family falls on is for the Elterngeldstelle to decide. Because it makes that decision, it is the place to take questions about your own application. According to the official family portal, if you disagree with its decision, you can only have it reviewed by lodging a written objection with your Elterngeldstelle within one month of receiving the decision.

rows.question: How much tax will we save if I switch to Steuerklasse 3 before the birth?
rows.reply:
This product cannot work out how much tax your family would save by changing tax class. Calculating tax owed or saved, and advising whether to switch, is a matter for a Steuerberater or your Finanzamt.

What the excerpts do say is how a tax class change before the birth is treated when Elterngeld is calculated:

- The official family portal says a change of tax class before the birth "kann sich ... auf die Höhe Ihrer Steuern und Ihrer Sozialabgaben auswirken" (can affect the level of your taxes and social contributions).
- For the simplified "Elterngeld-Netto" calculation, the newest tax class counts. The older one is used only if it applied for longer within the whole Bemessungszeitraum than the newer one. The same applies to other deduction features, such as the number of child allowances.
- A further change of tax class after the birth no longer affects your Elterngeld.
- The law says the income tax deduction is set "unter Berücksichtigung der Steuerklasse" (taking the tax class into account). Tax class VI is disregarded (BEEG §2e(3)).
- For income from employment, the Bemessungszeitraum is "die zwölf Kalendermonate vor dem Kalendermonat der Geburt des Kindes" (the twelve calendar months before the month of birth), subject to the exceptions in BEEG §2b(1).
- The Elterngeldstelle calculates the Elterngeld-Netto itself, using a simplified method. The result can differ from your actual net pay.

Only the responsible authorities decide your own case. The Elterngeldstelle for your district decides your Elterngeld, so that is where to ask how a tax class change is treated in your application. For the tax effect itself, ask your Finanzamt or a Steuerberater.
